core_obligations: Endow the closed subset Z with the reduced induced closed subscheme structure (proof lines 6737-6738).

For each member of the fpqc covering, identify the base change of Z with a closed subscheme of the base changed source having the given inverse image as underlying closed subset (proof lines 6739-6741).
Conclude from the definition, through the cited characterisation, that the projections from these base changes are proper (proof lines 6741-6743).
Apply the descent lemma for properness to obtain that the morphism from Z to the base is proper, and conclude that Z is proper over the base by definition (proof lines 6744-6746).
proof_roadmap: Put the reduced induced structure on Z (proof lines 6737-6738).
Identify the base changes as closed subschemes with the given underlying sets (proof lines 6739-6741).
Get properness of the base changed projections (proof lines 6741-6743).
Descend properness and read off the conclusion (proof lines 6744-6746).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism of schemes of locally finite type, a closed subset Z of the source is proper over the base as soon as its inverse image in the base change along some fpqc covering is (statement lines 6726-6734). The proof begins with a choice that makes the rest work: Z is endowed with the reduced induced closed subscheme structure, which is what turns a statement about a closed subset into a statement about a morphism of schemes (proof lines 6737-6738). For each member of the covering, the base change of Z is identified as a closed subscheme of the base changed source whose underlying closed subset is the given inverse image, and the definition of being proper over the base, by way of a cited lemma, gives that the projections from these base changes to the members of the covering are proper (proof lines 6739-6743). Properness of the morphism from Z to the base then descends by the earlier lemma on descending properness, and the conclusion for the closed subset follows from the definition (proof lines 6744-6746). The claim is H2: the reduction from a closed subset to its reduced induced scheme structure is a real step, the identification of the base changes has to be made, and the descent lemma is then applied to the resulting morphisms.
